messages:
nina: quick note — a new customer hit a confusing onboarding flow: the python sample app uses tool_call(output_type=MyDataclass) in async examples, but our docs only show output_type for sync calls. they tried the async sample and got TypeError on coroutine vs value.

nina: small excerpt from their copied sample: 

nina: ```py
from dataclasses import dataclass
from redwood import AsyncClient

client = AsyncClient(api_key=\"...\")

@dataclass
class UserProfile:
    id: str
    name: str
    score: float

# user copied this from quickstart but forgot await in their handler
profile = client.tool_call(
    \"get_profile\",
    input={\"id\": \"u1\"},
    output_type=UserProfile,
)
print(profile.name)  # TypeError: 'coroutine' object has no attribute 'name'
```

nina: they raised two asks: 1) docs should show async variants explicitly 2) typing for tool_call ergonomics — mypy/IDE inference is poor for tool_call return types in async contexts.

oscar: good catch. we didn't intentionally omit async docs, just an oversight. but the typing issue is real: our stub currently types tool_call as -> ToolCallResponse[Any] and only coerces at runtime; that means IDEs don't know the shaped type.

yuki: pattern i've used in other SDKs: provide overloads in stubs so tool_call(...) -> ToolCallResponse[T] and async def tool_call(...) -> ToolCallResponse[T] for sync vs async; plus a convenience awaitable wrapper so `await client.tool_call(..., output_type=UserProfile)` has proper typing.

yuki: example typing overloads in pyi: 

ny: (typo) -> ignore

yuki: ```py
from typing import TypeVar, Generic, Awaitable
T = TypeVar('T')
class ToolCallResponse(Generic[T]):
    parsed: T
    raw: str

# overloads
def tool_call(..., output_type: Type[T]) -> ToolCallResponse[T]: ...
async def tool_call(..., output_type: Type[T]) -> ToolCallResponse[T]: ...
# or: tool_call(...) -> Awaitable[ToolCallResponse[T]] for a single async signature
```

ben: another real DX snag: sample-apps use dataclasses for coercion but we don't document how optional fields, defaults, and extra keys are handled. customer had tool return extra fields and coercion crashed.

ben: propose we add a short table: dataclass->coercion rules: keep extra keys (store in __extras__?), missing required -> error unless strict=False, allow defaults to fill missing fields, support typing.Optional. and show examples.

nina: +1. also on onboarding: add an ESL example for common pitfalls: missing await, forgetting output_type, stringified json output from tools, and streaming differences (ndjson vs chunked frames). Customers copy-paste examples and then hit these edges.

oscar: for typing, we could also provide small helpers (in devex package) like parse_tool_response(resp, output_type=UserProfile) -> UserProfile with proper typing. That makes runtime coercion explicit and helps IDEs. But still want good overloads on client methods.

yuki: on the coercion crash: implement a coerce_mode param with values: 'strict','lenient'. lenient will ignore extra keys and try to coerce stringified json. strict raises on mismatches. default should be lenient to improve first-run experience.

ben: caveat: default lenient might hide errors for enterprise customers; we'll expose strict=True and recommend it for validation in CI/evals.

oscar: also add a lint rule in sample-app CI that runs a small smoke test asserting tool_call(...) returns a parsed object when using output_type in examples. That would have caught the missing-await bug in the repo before it reaches customers.

nina: tiny UX ask: include the SDK-generated request_id in the ToolCallResponse dataclass so that apps can log and correlate. right now it's only in debug logs.

doc-bot: created issue redwood/sdk#3720 \"docs: clarify async tool_call examples, typing overloads, and coercion rules\" (assigned to @oscar). https://github.com/redwood/sdk/issues/3720

yuki: implementation plan:
- add pyi overloads and update typing tests
- add parse_tool_response helper with runtime checks and typed return
- adjust default coerce_mode to 'lenient', add strict flag
- docs: quickstart async section with common pitfalls and example CI check
- sample-app: update examples, add smoke test for missing await and output_type correctness

ben: i'll PR small dataclass coercion spec and a sample test for extra keys vs strict mode. nina can add the docs quickstart snippet.

oscar: i'll own the typing PR and the pyi updates. will coordinate with yuki for helper API naming.

nina: thanks team. i'll loop in the support engineer who triaged the customer so we can verify the fix addresses their issues. :thumbsup:
